LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. 

The source definition uses a standard AUR-style URL pointing to the project's official domain (https://www.ireasoning.com/download/). This is a legitimate, non-mutated source that will be fetched during the build process. The SHA256 checksums are fully specified (none are marked SKIP), which is required for verified sources. Since the `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags prevent any code execution during these steps, the top-level PKGBUILD parsing and source extraction are purely read-only operations. There are no VCS references, no untrusted network endpoints, no shell command substitutions, and no code that could execute malicious payloads. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices with no signs of supply-chain compromise or backdoor mechanisms.

The only thing to note is that the source URL (https://www.ireasoning.com/download/) is external, but this is the official project repository and is explicitly allowed in AUR packaging. The checksum verification ensures integrity, and the absence of SKIP marks means the source is trusted. The `prepare()` and `package()` functions contain standard installation logic that runs after the build phase (which is skipped here), so they do not affect the current command sequence.

Overall, this PKGBUILD presents no security concerns for the narrow safety gate defined—only standard, expected AUR operations are performed.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

The source URL is from the official project domain, checksums are fully specified, and the --nobuild/--noprepare flags ensure no code execution occurs during the fetch phase.
